newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti says performance still negative.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti says performance still negative.

text.p: The chief executive of Italy's struggling hi-tech group Olivetti Francesco Caio said that the economic and financial performance of the company was still strongly negative.
Caio was giving testimony to the upper house Senate industry commission on Thursday.

Caio added that the performance of mobile phone group Omnitel, where Olivetti has a 41.3 percent stake, was above the company's own forecasts. The group launched its mobile phone service in December 1995 and at the end of August had 500,000 subscribers.

He said that he expects Olivetti's struggling PC company to have sales of 2 trillion lire or a little more in 1996, but confirmed that the PC company would not break even after it lost 200 billion lire in 1995 and 10 billion lire in the first half of 1996.
